description:
FILED s536e (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08) from its one-file companion acceptance run (scratch/s536e/comp.log, comp2.log in the s536e worktree).  NOT s536e's: main ba7863a3 and the s536e tree give the same answer; ATTRIBUTED by probing MAIN-READY-75 (33334fb1) vs MAIN-READY-76 (4651f35a = s536a merged).

REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3, scratch/s536e/pr/m6x.pl m6w.pl):

    my $w;
    sub oon::TIESCALAR{bless[],"oon"}
    sub oon::FETCH{$w++}
    tie my $t, "oon";
    push my @c, $t, 5; print "e w=$w\n"; $w=0;       # perl e w=1   PCL e w=2
    my @f = ($t, -e "/nonexist"); print "f w=$w\n";  # perl 1       PCL 1
    push my @a, $t;  # alone: perl 1, PCL 1

A `push` with MORE THAN ONE argument FETCHes a tied scalar argument TWICE (one argument, or a list assignment, fetches once).

WHY IT SHOWS NOW: perl's t/op/filetest.t row 277 "file test does not call FETCH on stack item not its own" (`push my @a, $t, -t`) passed in the companion snapshot (375/61) by an ACCIDENT: before MAIN-READY-76 a push stored the tied proxy without FETCHing it at all (MAIN-READY-75: `push my @a, $t` -> w=0; `push my @c, $t, -e ...` -> w=1, which happened to equal perl).  s536a's #4183 / #1814 fix (a tied scalar copied into an aggregate is its FETCHed value, once) made the copy FETCH -- and the multi-argument push path FETCHes a second time.  op/filetest.t 375/61 -> 374/62 on main; the row is left for the round attribution (baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv header note, s536e).

FIX DIRECTION (not read): the multi-argument `p-push` (or its argument flattening) reads the tied value once to build the list and again on store; the single-argument path and `%p-array-store-scalar` (s536a) fetch once -- make the multi-argument path hand the already-FETCHed value to the store.  Bar: the reproducer = perl; op/filetest.t row 277 passes for the right reason; t/op/tie*.t one-file runs unmoved.  Also seen on the way, not this: a bare `-t` lowers to `(p--t $_)` where perl's `-t` tests STDIN (the `$_`-default pre-pass treats `-t` like the other filetests).

=== DONE (s537a, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-10 .. 11-13; commit 44c083c6 on the s537a branch, rebased over MAIN-READY-87; shas as of the rebase over main b620405f) ===
FIXED: `p-push-impl` classified each item with `(unbox item)` (FETCH 1) and then stored it through `%p-array-store-scalar` (FETCH 2).  It now PEEKS the box's value slot -- p-unshift's #1814 rule -- so the store's read is the only one: `push my @c, $t, 5` 2 -> 1 FETCH (perl 1), `push @b, 5, $t, $t` 4 -> 2 (perl 2).  ir-spec §2.2b rule 8 gains the sentence.  Break shapes probed identical to main (scratch/s537a/p/m5d.pl: push @b / %h / qw / a ref / $1 $& / $#b / a list-returning call / @{$c[0]} / sort / substr / lc / $_ ); one PRE-EXISTING divergence found there and filed: #4805 (`push @n, @n, @n`).
GUARD: Pl/t/tie-fetch-once-01.t program 5 rows 31-33 (inverse on main: 31 32 fail).  Targeted gate tg56 47 files / 2481 PASS.  Companion one-file op/filetest.t (row 277) + op/tie*.t: see the session log's Bars line.
BARS (the combined tree over MAIN-READY-87, HEAD 7cd511ac): FULL gate 369 / 12,018 -> 12,046 PASS (+ tr-01.t row 9 = 12,047); FULL sweep GATE clean 0 new / 0 fixed / 0 LOST, TOTAL 18,795 -> 18,796 (tr.t +1 = #1493, by edit), drops 5 = census; corpus-diff vs 23f0f917 3 / 111; wide emission A/B 2,053 files 29 DIFF explained / RCDIFF 0; gate-SET scan 638 files IDENTICAL over both populations; ir-host-leak 31 = 31; ir-conform 328 / 0; EVERYDAY 116 -> 116 of 122 (NEW 0); compile time unchanged (Calc.pm 5.52 -> 5.51 s).  Detail: docs/session-log.md, section s537a.
